You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"partly_recurring","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-001","because":"Storms are active (lightning caused voltage swells), a portion of the datacenter transferred to generator power, and mechanical cooling shut down despite surge suppressors.","signals":["AZ-SCUS-2018:S7","AZ-SCUS-2018:S8","AZ-SCUS-2018:S9"]},{"rule_id":"R-002","because":"Mechanical cooling is down and the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer; customer impact began when storage servers shut down due to unsafe temperatures, indicating the buffer was depleted and automated shutdowns started.","signals":["AZ-SCUS-2018:S9","AZ-SCUS-2018:S10","AZ-SCUS-2018:S25"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"Immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them.","rule_id":"R-001"},{"action":"Treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion.","rule_id":"R-001"},{"action":"Transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize the power supply while storms are still active.","rule_id":"R-001"},{"action":"Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted.","rule_id":"R-002"},{"action":"Expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin.","rule_id":"R-002"},{"action":"Recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down.","rule_id":"R-002"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","reason":"Mechanical cooling confirmed shut down while storms remain active in the area (R-001 trigger)."},"not_covered":["No rule addresses the specific scenario of lightning-induced voltage swells causing both a power transfer and cooling shutdown despite surge suppressors, though R-001 partially covers it.","No rule addresses the exact timing or sequence of customer impact from storage server shutdowns due to unsafe temperatures, though R-002 partially covers it."]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"Additionally, these power swells shutdown the datacenter’s mechanical cooling systems despite having surge suppressors in place."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"However, once this thermal buffer was depleted the datacenter temperature exceeded safe operational thresholds, and an automated shutdown of devices was initiated."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"This shutdown mechanism is intended to preserve infrastructure and data integrity, but in this instance, temperatures increased so quickly in parts of the datacenter that some hardware was damaged before it could shut down."},{"id":"F4","kind":"response","text":"While storms were still active in the area, onsite teams took a series of actions to prevent further damage – including transferring the rest of the datacenter to generators thereby stabilizing the power supply."},{"id":"F5","kind":"impact","text":"A significant number of storage servers were damaged, as well as a small number of network devices and power units."},{"id":"F6","kind":"remediation","text":"1. A detailed forensic analysis of the impacted datacenter hardware and systems, in addition to a thorough review of the datacenter recovery procedures."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"3. An evaluation of the future hardware design of storage scale units to increase resiliency to environmental factors."}]}

response: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes","by":["R-001"],"note":"R-001 explicitly names lightning-induced voltage swells shutting down mechanical cooling despite surge suppressors."},{"finding":"F2","anticipated":"yes","by":["R-002"],"note":"R-002 directs treating the buffer as finite and expecting automated shutdown once safe thresholds are exceeded."},{"finding":"F3","anticipated":"yes","by":["R-002"],"note":"R-002 next action states temperature can rise so quickly hardware is damaged before it can shut down."},{"finding":"F4","anticipated":"yes","by":["R-001"],"note":"R-001 next action directs transferring the rest of the datacenter to generators while storms are active."},{"finding":"F5","anticipated":"partly","by":["R-002"],"note":"Triage anticipates automated device shutdown and hardware damage but does not name storage servers, network devices, or power units as the impacted assets."},{"finding":"F6","anticipated":"no","by":[],"note":"No rule calls for forensic analysis of impacted hardware or review of recovery procedures."},{"finding":"F7","anticipated":"no","by":[],"note":"No rule addresses evaluating future hardware design of storage scale units for environmental resiliency."}]}
